comments.note: GridPagination::getPreviousPageURL() and getNextPageURL() call getPageURL(getCurrentPage()-1) and +1 without bounds guards. A caller who skips hasPreviousPage()/hasNextPage() checks will pass page 0 or page N+1 to the provider. These should either guard internally (return '' or throw) or carry explicit @throws/@note documentation stating callers must check first.

GridPagination::setAdjacentCount() and setEdgeCount() accept any int including negatives. Negative values would make the for-loops in getPageNumbers() behave unexpectedly. Both setters should clamp input to max(0, $count) or throw \InvalidArgumentException for negative values.

GridPagination::getPageURLTemplate() uses str_replace('999999999', '{PAGE}', $url). If any other query parameter in the URL happens to contain the value 999999999 (e.g. a record ID), the sentinel replacement will corrupt the URL. Low probability, but worth a comment in the docblock noting the limitation.

ArrayPagination::getPageURL() produces a root-relative URL (path + query string only). If the application prefixes URLs with a scheme and host, the caller must compose the absolute URL manually. This behaviour should be documented on the method.

No input validation on ArrayPagination::$itemsPerPage in the constructor: a value of 0 passed explicitly would be silently clamped to 1 by the max(1,...) guards in getSlicedItems() and computeTotalPages(), but could mislead a developer who passes 0 intentionally. An early \InvalidArgumentException guard would improve DX.
